verdict.rationale: Temporal's Client API lets application code start or signal Workflow Executions in response to app events (temporal-docs-50, temporal-docs-6/38), and Activities/child workflows let a single Workflow fan out to many functions (temporal-docs-3, temporal-docs-35); Schedules cover time-based triggers (temporal-docs-5, temporal-docs-23). However this is done via imperative SDK calls in your own event/webhook/queue handler, not a native declarative trigger binding, and no first-party webhook/queue-connector or explicit fan-out pattern documentation is present. Missing for 10: documented native webhook/queue ingestion connectors, a declarative event-trigger config (vs code-driven client calls), and explicit fan-out-to-many-activities examples/docs.
